language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi, I'm Ruth, and I've come with my Mom to buy some vegetables but I'm bored.
The wheel of that rickshaw looks fascinating. If I look at it's spokes, it forms various angles. Did you know there are various types of angles?
A right angle is 90 degrees. An acute angle is less than 90 degrees.
An obtuse angle measures greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees. A straight angle measures 180 degrees, that's actually just a straight line.
When you bend a line past this point you call it a reflex angle, but that just looks like a smaller angle the other way around.
Can you help Ruth learn the various types of angles?

An angle is made up of two arms.
Here line OP and line OR are the arms of the angle. Point O is where the two lines meet and it is called the vertex.
When measuring angles, you place the protractor on the vertex so that one of the lines of the angle you want to measure reads zero.
Read the number of the protractor where the second side of the angle meets the protractor. In this case the angle measures 90 degrees and is a right angle.
